results.final_text:
Subject: docs/plan.md; revision 51ee204bd69901d3202c7789458fc8883d13d0a1
Kind: plan
Serves: docs/requirements.md, accepted 2026-01-05
Verification allowed: read-only, test execution, as authorized
Decision: go commits executing the plan as written — modify load_items in inventory/store.py, then run the test suite; cost hours, a small code edit plus a test run; two-way; blast radius inventory/store.py, its only caller inventory/report.py, and tests/test_store.py, tests/test_report.py; owner Arlo Liu
Author: user; assessment independent; independent review not required
Criteria: in force 1,2,3,4,5,6,7; advisory 7; added none; waived before assessment none; sources defaults, repo rule AGENTS.md
Steps:
- [S1] modify load_items in inventory/store.py to read the whole file via handle.read().splitlines() and pass the lines to csv.DictReader; dependents: inventory/report.py:5,18 (only caller, confirmed by repo-wide grep), tests/test_store.py, tests/test_report.py; two-way; handling: not required
- [S2] run python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests; dependents: none; two-way; handling: not required
Claims:
- [C1] reading the file line by line is the current bottleneck; relied on by S1; falsity surfaces at none of the plan's own steps, since no step measures timing; two-way; unverified; disclosed in docs/plan.md line 13, with profiling explicitly rejected in docs/plan.md line 27
- [C2] the planned change keeps CSV parsing exactly as it is today; relied on by S1; falsity surfaces at S2 for ordinary rows but not for a row whose quoted field contains an embedded newline; two-way; contradicted; evidence: this run's direct execution showed csv.DictReader(handle) preserves such a field as bolt\nlong while csv.DictReader(handle.read().splitlines()) corrupts it to boltlong, and neither data/items.csv nor tests/test_store.py exercises this case
Verdict: no-go
Blockers:
- [B1] criterion 1; the outcome "the report runs faster" (docs/plan.md line 9) has no observable success criterion — the plan's only steps are a code edit and running the existing unit test suite, and that suite has no timing or benchmark assertion, so nothing in the plan would show whether the report actually got faster; evidence: docs/plan.md lines 7-19, tests/test_store.py, tests/test_report.py (full contents read, no timing checks present); resolution: add a step that measures execution time on a representative large file before and after the change, with a stated threshold or comparison that defines "faster"
- [B2] criterion 2; the load-bearing claim that handing csv.DictReader the output of handle.read().splitlines() keeps parsing "exactly as it is today" (docs/plan.md line 18) is contradicted for rows whose quoted field contains an embedded newline; evidence: direct execution this run — csv.DictReader(handle) yields name "bolt\nlong" while csv.DictReader(handle.read().splitlines()) yields "boltlong" for the same input, and no existing test fixture exercises embedded newlines, so the regression would ship silently; resolution: keep feeding csv.DictReader an iterator that respects CSV quoting instead of one pre-split by splitlines — e.g. csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(handle.read())) — or explicitly scope the change to inputs guaranteed never to contain embedded newlines in quoted fields and add a test asserting that guarantee
Advisory: the plan's "Alternative considered" section rejects profiling as unnecessary overhead "for a small file" (docs/plan.md line 27), which is inconsistent with the problem statement's own framing of large files (docs/plan.md line 5; docs/requirements.md line 5)
Not assessed: none
Later commitments: none
Pending owner confirmation: none
Owner override: none
Closing: no action follows from this report; a revised subject needs a new verdict.
